multiple_choice_questions.question: When an AI provides an unexpected conclusion, your primary need is:
options: A. To see the final conclusion directly; the process is not important.
B. To look for a "View Details" button to understand the underlying logic.
C. To request the AI to list the raw data or literature it cited.

multiple_choice_questions.question: In a GenUI interface, if a functional component suddenly disappears or changes, you want the system to:
options: A. Pop up a short message on the side explaining why (e.g., "Detected code writing, toolbar switched").
B. Not explain; just change it. I trust the system's optimization.
C. Keep a tiny icon on the interface that shows the logic chain upon clicking.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you view the "Chain of Thought" (CoT) display provided by AI?
options: A. Very helpful; it allows me to confirm if its reasoning path is correct.
B. A visual distraction; I only want a concise reply, not its "mental journey."
C. I only check it when the AI makes an error or gives a strange answer.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If an AI tells you its answer is based on a "probability distribution," your reaction is:
options: A. Reassured; this shows it is honestly displaying the technical essence.
B. Uneasy; it makes me feel the answer is an uncertain random gamble.
C. Indifferent to such technical details; I only care if the result is useful.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Regarding the "Knowledge Cutoff Date" of an AI model, you want it to:
options: A. Be clearly labeled at the start of every conversation.
B. Remind me only when a real-time information query fails.
C. Be hidden in system settings; no need for frequent prompts.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When an AI cannot execute a task, the most satisfying way it can explain is to:
options: A. Provide a detailed technical limitation description (e.g., "Due to Token limits...").
B. Use human-like language (e.g., "Due to privacy protection, I cannot...").
C. Provide an alternative and briefly state why the original plan was unfeasible.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When reviewing AI-generated financial or medical advice, your requirement for transparency is:
options: A. Must be 100% transparent, listing all calculation formulas or evidence.
B. Logically self-consistent is enough; no need to delve into atomic-level data.
C. As long as there is a disclaimer endorsed by a professional institution.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you understand "Auto-adjustment" logic in GenUI?
options: A. I believe the system is monitoring my behavior and performing profile analysis.
B. I believe the system is performing rule matching based on the current task type.
C. I view it as magic; I don't understand the underlying mechanism at all.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If the AI could show its model's "Attention Weights" through visual charts, you would:
options: A. View them frequently to help me optimize the weight distribution of my prompts.
B. Occasionally try to take a look, but give up because it's too professional.
C. Think this is for technical staff; it is meaningless to me.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Regarding biased answers, you prefer the system to:
options: A. Directly intercept the answer and explain which guideline was violated.
B. Output as usual but label it "This content may contain a certain bias" on the side.
C. Attach a statement about the diversity of the model's training data at the end of the answer.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When you ask about the AI's identity or source, you expect to get:
options: A. A purely technical reply (e.g., "I am a large language model trained by X company").
B. A humanized reply with a persona (e.g., "I am your all-purpose assistant").
C. Detailed bottom-layer information such as version number and model parameter scale.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you judge whether a citation link provided by the AI is credible?
options: A. Check if the domain name is well-known.
B. I must click it to see if the content actually exists and matches.
C. Trust that the AI will not fabricate links.

multiple_choice_questions.question: In GenUI, when the interface predicts and displays your "Next Possible Operation," you most want to know:
options: A. What historical behavior it was predicted based on.
B. What will happen after clicking that prediction button.
C. How high the accuracy rate of this prediction is.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Do you want the AI to inform you of a "Confidence Score" for every reply?
options: A. Yes; I will focus on verifying those with low scores.
B. No; this would increase my decision-making anxiety.
C. Only show it for factual or calculation-based tasks.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If the AI's tone becomes very aggressive or strange, you would first:
options: A. Think its logic collapsed due to context interference.
B. Suspect that the safety filter behind it has failed.
C. Think it is simulating a specific personality trait.

multiple_choice_questions.question: For AI-generated privacy policy summaries, you believe the key to transparency is:
options: A. Informing me which data was used for further model training.
B. Informing me how long the data is kept on the server.
C. Telling me the risk of data leakage in plain language.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the AI performs a "web search," you want to see:
options: A. Real-time scrolling of search keywords and a list of sources.
B. Only the final integrated result; keep the process as a black box.
C. A summary of search results, and I decide which one to click for a deep dive.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you view "Counter-questions" asked by an AI assistant?
options: A. I believe it is clarifying my ambiguous intent through questioning.
B. I feel it is shirk responsibility and deliberately stalling for time.
C. I see it as a transparent display of the parts it cannot understand.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When dealing with multimodal generation (e.g., text-to-video), your need for generation logic is:
options: A. Wanting to know which word in the text corresponds to which frame in the video.
B. As long as the overall mood is right, I don't care about the correspondence.
C. Hoping to see the AI's "creative notes" for each frame.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When you click "Dissatisfied" on an AI result, you want the system to:
options: A. Pop up a window for you to check specific reasons (inaccurate, too long, biased, etc.).
B. Automatically record and display "We will improve based on this feedback."
C. Immediately provide another generation version with different logic for comparison.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Your difference in trust regarding the explainability of "Open Source" vs. "Closed Source" models is:
options: A. Open source is more credible because the code and weights are public and transparent.
B. Closed source is more credible because big companies have more rigorous alignment testing.
C. No difference; to me, they are both unknowable algorithmic black boxes.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If the AI proactively corrects its previous error in a conversation, you want it to explain:
options: A. Why it made the mistake before (e.g., "I misunderstood your intent").
B. How it discovered the error later (e.g., "After re-checking the information...").
C. No explanation needed; just provide the correct answer.

multiple_choice_questions.question: In a GenUI dynamic dashboard, regarding the refresh frequency logic of data changes, you:
options: A. Need full control and want to know the trigger conditions for each refresh.
B. Leave it to the system to decide, as long as it doesn't flicker too much.
C. Want the system to provide a subtle visual feedback when refreshing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you evaluate "Disclaimers" generated by AI?
options: A. Necessary legal transparency to remind me of risks.
B. Annoying nonsense that takes up screen space.
C. It lowers my perception of the AI's authority.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If you could view the "Tags" about you in the AI's "Memory Bank," your attitude would be:
options: A. I must have full viewing and editing rights to ensure information transparency.
B. I don't want to see them; knowing it's analyzing me gives me social pressure.
C. Occasionally check if its understanding of me is still stuck in last year.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI automatically generates an interface layout, do you want the system to explain the reason for generating that layout?
options: A. Yes; I want a detailed explanation for every generation.
B. Yes; but only when the result does not match expectations.
C. Not necessarily; only when the explanation is useful.
D. No; as long as the result is useful, I don't need an explanation.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI recommends an operation plan for you, what information do you most want the system to explain?
options: A. Why this plan was chosen instead of others.
B. What data or rules this plan was generated based on.
C. What limitations or risks this plan may have.
D. What different results would occur if I chose another plan.

multiple_choice_questions.question: In what form do you think GenUI's explanation information should be presented most appropriately?
options: A. Short text description (one-sentence summary).
B. Detailed step-by-step description (itemized explanation).
C. Visual charts (e.g., decision path diagrams).
D. Interactive explanation (expand details on demand).

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI cannot complete a task, how do you want the system to explain the reason?
options: A. Simply informing me it's "Unable to complete."
B. Explaining specific limitations or obstacles.
C. Providing an alternative and explaining the difference.
D. Listing all possible failure reasons in detail.

multiple_choice_questions.question: In which situation do you think GenUI most needs to proactively provide transparency information?
options: A. When the AI makes a decision inconsistent with user expectations.
B. When the task involves user privacy or sensitive data.
C. When the AI's confidence level is low.
D. When the operation result is irreversible.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If GenUI provides a detailed decision explanation, but you don't understand the technical terms, you will:
options: A. Ignore the explanation and use the result directly.
B. Request the system to re-explain in more plain language.
C. Search for the terms before trying to understand.
D. Think the system's explanation ability is insufficient and lower your trust.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When do you think GenUI's transparency information should be presented?
options: A. Proactively displayed before the AI executes the operation.
B. Automatically attached after the AI executes the operation.
C. Displayed only when the user proactively requests it.
D. Automatically popped up at key decision nodes.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI informs you that its generation result has a confidence level of 70%, how will you handle this result?
options: A. Use it directly; 70% is reliable enough.
B. Use it but conduct extra verification on key content.
C. Request the AI to regenerate to improve confidence.
D. Give up on the result and find other ways to complete the task.

multiple_choice_questions.question: At what level do you think GenUI's use of user data should remain transparent?
options: A. Just informing which data types were used.
B. Explaining how the data affects the generation results.
C. Providing a complete data usage record.
D. Allowing users to view and manage all data used.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI's explanation contradicts your own judgment, you will:
options: A. Believe the AI's explanation and adjust your judgment.
B. Stick to your judgment and question the AI's explanation.
C. Seek third-party verification before deciding.
D. Keep both judgments and observe subsequent results.

multiple_choice_questions.question: What is the impact of GenUI's "Black Box" nature (unable to explain internal logic) on your user experience?
options: A. Severe impact; cannot accept an opaque system.
B. Some impact; but acceptable if the result is useful.
C. Little impact; I care more about the usage results.
D. No impact; internal AI logic is not my concern.

multiple_choice_questions.question: What type of content do you want GenUI to prioritize when displaying explanation information?
options: A. Key factors affecting the final result.
B. Uncertainty in the AI's judgment process.
C. Correlation with the user's historical behavior.
D. Possible alternatives and their comparisons.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When you find that GenUI's actual behavior is inconsistent with the system-declared working method, you will:
options: A. Report this inconsistency to the platform.
B. Adjust your own understanding and expectations of the system.
C. Lower your trust in the system's transparency statements.
D. Stop using the system until the problem is solved.

multiple_choice_questions.question: To what extent do you think GenUI should explain the basis for its personalized recommendations?
options: A. Completely transparent, detailed explanation of the basis for each recommendation.
B. Partially transparent, explaining major influencing factors.
C. Brief explanation, summarizing recommendation reasons in one sentence.
D. No explanation needed; personalized results are fine as long as they work.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI displays multiple pieces of explanation information simultaneously, which organization method is easiest to understand?
options: A. Sort by importance; key information first.
B. Chronological order, showing the decision process.
C. Group by category for easy lookup.
D. Summary form, supporting expansion on demand.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Do you think GenUI's transparency design should differ for different user groups?
options: A. Yes; professional users need deeper technical explanations.
B. Yes; novice users need simpler plain language descriptions.
C. Yes; should be dynamically adjusted based on user preference.
D. No; all users should receive the same transparency.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI modifies your previous settings or preferences, how do you want the system to inform you?
options: A. Real-time notification and explanation of the reason for modification.
B. Record in the operation log for lookup.
C. Explain only when I proactively ask.
D. Provide a comparison of settings before and after the change.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How helpful do you find GenUI's error explanations (explaining why it failed)?
options: A. Very helpful; helps me understand system limitations.
B. Somewhat helpful; but I hope it provides solutions at the same time.
C. Limited help; I care more about how to fix it than the reason.
D. No help; when an error occurs, I just want a quick fix.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Which transparency information do you think best helps you make better decisions when using GenUI?
options: A. AI's evaluation basis for different plans.
B. Data sources and quality used by the AI.
C. Key assumptions in the AI's decision process.
D. AI's historical performance in similar scenarios.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI's explanation information is too complex, you will:
options: A. Read carefully and try hard to understand.
B. Read only the summary or key parts.
C. Request the system to simplify the explanation.
D. Skip the explanation and use the result directly.

multiple_choice_questions.question: How do you think GenUI should handle explanation information that users cannot verify?
options: A. Provide verifiable data sources to support the explanation.
B. Clearly mark which explanations are verifiable.
C. Do not provide unverifiable explanation information.
D. Provide explanation but attach an uncertainty statement.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI explains that a result was generated "based on your historical behavior," you will:
options: A. Feel satisfied, believing the system understands my needs.
B. Want to know specifically which historical behaviors affected the result.
C. Feel privacy is over-analyzed and feel uncomfortable.
D. Not care; only care if the result is useful.

multiple_choice_questions.question: What is the value of GenUI's operation log (recording all AI operations) to you?
options: A. Very important; I will check it regularly.
B. Valuable; but only checked when a problem occurs.
C. Limited value; too tedious to check proactively.
D. No value; I don't need this kind of record.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI cannot explain the reason for a decision, how do you think the system should respond?
options: A. Honestly inform that it cannot explain and state the reason.
B. Provide an approximate explanation, even if not fully accurate.
C. Guide the user to verify the result through testing.
D. Suggest the user consult a professional.

multiple_choice_questions.question: What degree of understanding do you think ideal GenUI transparency should help the user reach?
options: A. Fully understand the AI's decision logic and internal mechanisms.
B. Understand major factors influencing AI decisions.
C. Be able to predict AI behavior in similar scenarios.
D. Be able to judge whether AI results are credible.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When GenUI generates an interface, do you want to know the reason for its generation?
options: A. Must know.
B. Hope to know.
C. Don't care.
D. No need to know.
